text.p: Macquarie Equities has put a sell rating on Fletcher Challenge Ltd's paper division, which is listed as one of Fletcher's four 'letter' stocks.
Macquarie said in a report to clients that Fletcher Challenge Paper, as the world's largest newsprint producer, was vulnerable to an apparent ongoing collapse in newsprint prices.
"Just like the collapse in pulp markets 12 months ago, the severity and the speed of the collapse in newsprint prices may be underestimated by the market," Macquarie said.
Macquarie said Fletcher's newsprint earnings were NZ$139 million in the second half of the year to June 30, 1996 against NZ$204 million in the first half.
"With recent falls in newsprint prices, next year will not look so good," Macquarie said.
Since April newsprint prices had only fallen around 15 percent from their peak to about US$600 per tonne, whereas pulp prices had fallen 50 percent from their peaks.
"These (newsprint prices) are now forecast to fall to US$500 per tonne by December," Macquarie analyst Phil King said.
Newsprint inventories at both mills and publishers remained relatively high and although newsprint consumption in Asia was growing, consumption in developed countries was dropping off.
"This trend could accelerate with changing leisure habits and increased use of the internet as a medium," King said.
Newsprint production capacity was also growing, particularly in Asia, where capacity was forecast to grow 11 percent in both 1996 and 1997.
Fletcher Paper's share price was down one cent at A$2.76 at (1.29 p.m. (0325 GMT).
